Pick a controversial issue - something people clearly agree or disagree with strongly, like global warming.

Pollution has become a major issue facing the international community. However, dealing with recycling, waste treatment, and soil and water contamination is not a new phenomenon.
Conferences and international summits are regularly held to discuss the need for greater commitments by nations and to recognize the impact of human waste on the natural environment.
Indeed, an international approach, that will provide joint efforts between nations, is paramount in the fight against pollution.
Governments should be proactive and offer support to companies and organizations that are involved in manufacturing, industry or agriculture in order to encourage environmentally-friendly approaches.

We have developed the means to change our current trajectory with modern technology and require a shift in social values.
These could be introduced as special laws, certificates, tax incentives and recycling programs. However, this epidemic is not only the responsibility of country leaders. Individuals must also share in the responsibility. In the past, people might not have thought about their negative impact on the planet or may have considered the problem to be too big to think about. Yet, simple acts like switching off appliances and personal items can make significant differences over time.

People, who have tended to avoid recycling in the past, should think about separating waste materials and encouraging recycling practices. Furthermore, individuals who have previously used private vehicles, should consider using public transport as an environmentally-friendly alternative.  What it amounts to is making conscious choices about how you want to affect your surrounding. We mustn't let our selfishness dictate the future of others.  To sum up, environmental problems are everyone's responsibility.  Both local and international authorities as well as individuals need to make a concerted effort to minimize society's imprint on nature and preserve our planet for future generations.

Writing Tips for the Present Perfect
You can use the Present Perfect tense to talk about an event in the past that occurred at an unimportant or unknown time.
The Present Perfect is formed in the following manner:

Note: Sometimes the past participle form of the verb is the same as the past simple form of the verb.

I have visited many countries.
I visited many countries in 2007.
Sometimes the past participle form of the verb is different from the past simple form of the verb.

Vanessa has seen that movie three times.
Vanessa saw that movie yesterday.
The Present Perfect can provide a specific starting time or a duration of time only if for or since is used.

For example:

She has lived in Chicago for ten years.
She has lived in Chicago since 2005.
Look at the following examples from the text:
Pollution has become a major issue facing the international community.
Conferences and international summits are regularly held to discuss the need for greater commitments by nations and to recognize the impact of human waste on the natural environment.
We have developed the means to change our current trajectory with modern technology and require a shift in social values.
Since major recycling initiatives were introduced, there has been little change in the amount of garbage being produced.
You can provide extra information about someone or something by using a relative clause. Be careful though because a relative clause can not be used on its own. This will create a sentence fragment.
A relative clause provides additional information. It does not express a complete thought. As a result a relative clause must always be used in combination with a main clause.
Nolan took the bicycle which his brother had loaned him.
His brother had loaned him.
Xavier gave a gift to his brother, who thanked him profusely.
Who thanked him profusely.
A relative clause can contain essential information or non-essential information.
If a relative clause contains essential information, then a comma is not needed.
The man who delivered the newspaper was late.
If a relative clause contains non-essential information, then a comma is needed.
My father, who was born in 1962, worked as a machinist.
